overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Board's unnoticed vaccine-mandate discussion and vote were unanticipated by the Chair 48 hours ahead and raised by a member of the public. A second allegation about discussing an employee's vaccination status was declined as outside the law. The AG urged postponing unlisted controversial topics as best practice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed and voted on a COVID-19 vaccine mandate for Town employees at its August 25 meeting, a topic not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the topic of the vaccine mandate was raised by a member of the pubic at the August 25 meeting and the Board’s discussion and vote regarding the vaccine mandate was unanticipated by the Chair 48 hours prior to the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Board members discussed a Town employee's vaccination status during the August 25 open session meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
